title: SvidSigner private key material is never zeroized
description:
persona-core/src/signer.rs:55-61:

    pub struct SvidSigner {
        key_pair: EcdsaKeyPair,
        rng: SystemRandom,
        public_key_der: Vec<u8>,
        /// PKCS#8 DER bytes kept for jsonwebtoken ES256 signing.
        pkcs8_der: Vec<u8>,
    }

`pkcs8_der` is the full PKCS#8 DER of the P-256 private key, held in a plain `Vec<u8>` with no `Drop` impl and no `Zeroizing` wrapper. When `SvidSigner` is dropped the allocation is freed with the private scalar still in it. The doc comment on the struct says "The keypair is never persisted; it is discarded when the process exits" — "discarded" is not what `Vec::drop` does.

Concretely: the key survives in freed heap memory and can reach a core dump, a swap page, or a later heap allocation in the same process. Two copies exist (`pkcs8_der` plus whatever `EcdsaKeyPair` holds internally), and `SvidSigner::new()` at line 67-70 creates a third short-lived one — the `pkcs8` `Document` returned by `generate_pkcs8`, which is `.to_vec()`'d and then dropped un-zeroized at end of scope.

This is a daemon whose entire security argument rests on the ephemeral CA key not escaping the process, so the gap is worth closing even though ring's own `Document` handling is outside our control.

Fix: add `zeroize` and hold the field as `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`, or store the `EncodingKey` built once at construction and drop the DER immediately. Note `EncodingKey::from_ec_der` is called on every `sign_jwt_svid` (line 110) — building it once in `new()` removes the need to keep the DER around at all, which is the better fix.
